findings.quote: FY26 net income was $120.1 billion on a 63.7% net margin, figures more typical of software than of a hardware company.
findings.issue: 63.7% is the trailing-twelve-month net margin on the Facts surface ("Trailing twelve months ... Net margin 63.7%"), not FY26. FY26 net margin is 55.6% ($120.1B net income / $215.9B revenue). The same sentence correctly labels gross margin "71.1% for FY26 and 74.7% on a trailing basis" and operating margin "65.2% trailing," then attaches the trailing net margin to FY26 - a figure carried at the wrong period.
findings.fix: Label the net margin as trailing ("a 63.7% net margin on a trailing basis"), consistent with how gross and operating margin are split in the same sentence. Do not present the TTM net margin as the FY26 figure; the FY26 net margin (55.6%) is not on the surface, so quote only the trailing figure.
findings.note: Addressed. incomeCommentary reads "operating margin is 65.2% and net margin 63.7% on a trailing basis," with FY26 net income $120.1B stated separately and no net-margin figure attached to FY26.

findings.quote: the company has begun raising debt again, issuing bonds in the June quarter, not because it needs the money but to fund shareholder returns and the strategic financing arrangements it is extending to customers.
findings.issue: No bond issuance appears anywhere on the grounding surface - "bond" and "senior notes" occur zero times in the Facts or Context. The only debt data is the annual balance sheet (Total Debt $10.3B FY25 to $11.4B FY26), a fiscal year that ended January 2026, before the Q2 FY27 quarter ended 2026-07-26. Both the event ("issuing bonds in the June quarter") and its stated purpose are unsupported inferences.
findings.fix: Delete the bond-issuance claim and its rationale, or replace it with a grounded balance-sheet fact: Total Debt rose from $10.3B in FY25 to $11.4B in FY26 while Net Debt fell to $807M. Do not assert a Q2 bond issuance the pack does not carry.
findings.note: Addressed. The bond-issuance sentence is gone; balanceCommentary rests on cash-vs-debt, the trailing current ratio 4.59 and interest coverage over 400x.

findings.quote: receivables and inventory have swelled as revenue has exploded, a normal feature of hypergrowth but one to monitor for any sign that demand is being pulled forward.
findings.issue: The surface carries no receivables figure and no inventory balance; the balance-sheet block lists only cash, total debt, net debt, equity and current ratio. "Inventory" appears on the surface only as "increased inventory provisions" and "excess inventory" in the MD&A, never as a balance-sheet increase, and receivables are never mentioned. Asserting that both "have swelled" is a statement of fact the pack does not support.
findings.fix: Remove the claim, or tie the working-capital-monitoring point to a captured figure - e.g., the current ratio (4.59 TTM, down from 4.44 in FY25) - rather than to receivables and inventory movements the pack does not report.
findings.note: Addressed. The receivables/inventory sentence is removed; balanceCommentary uses only the captured current ratio (4.59 TTM).

findings.quote: a probability-weighted fair value of $260.50, about 23% above the price
findings.issue: The weighted fair value and upside ("$260.50 ... about/roughly 23% above the price") is stated three times in prose - analystCommentary, valuation.scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[0] - rather than argued once and referred back to in words. Separately, the FY26 buyback "$40.1 billion" is repeated in both financials.cashflowCommentary and management.capitalAllocation. Rubric 7: introduce a figure once and refer back in words.
findings.fix: Argue the $260.50 / 23% figure once, in the valuation section that derives it, and refer back to it in words in the analyst commentary and final recommendation instead of restating the number. Cite the $40.1B buyback in one of the two financials/management sections and refer back in the other.
findings.note: Addressed. $260.50/23% appears only in the analyst-commentary lead and the valuation section that derives it (summary-plus-derivation); finalRecommendation refers in words ("sits comfortably above the price"). The $40.1B buyback appears once (cashflowCommentary); capitalAllocation refers in words.

findings.quote: the June quarter's revenue of $96.2 billion was up 106% year-over-year
findings.issue: The reporting period is fiscal Q2 FY27, ended 2026-07-26 (late July), which the surface labels "Q2'27 (ended 2026-07-26)." "The June quarter" is used five times (financials.incomeCommentary, balanceCommentary, cashflowCommentary; businessMoat Data Center segment; growth point 1) and misnames a quarter that ended in late July.
findings.fix: Refer to it as the July quarter, the second quarter, or Q2'27 (ended July 26, 2026), consistently across all five occurrences.
findings.note: Addressed. "June quarter" no longer appears (0 occurrences); the period is called "the second quarter" throughout.

findings.quote: NVIDIA's income statement is one of the most remarkable in the market.
findings.issue: Several unearned superlatives the surface does not support: "one of the most remarkable in the market" (incomeCommentary), "The moat is the deepest in technology" (businessMoat Data Center segment), "the widest in the industry" (businessMoat.durability), "one of the most successful leadership records in business" (management.leadership), and "The outlook is huge" (growth point 4). House style bars unearned superlatives and hype and asks the numbers to carry the weight.
findings.fix: Remove or soften each: state the margin and growth figures without "most remarkable"; rely on the WIDE moatRating without "deepest/widest in the industry"; drop "huge" and "most successful leadership records in business."
findings.note: Addressed. No unearned superlatives remain: growth point 4 "strong but supply-limited," leadership "record is exceptional," income "stands apart." Remaining "extraordinary scale" and "deepest moat" are the earned magnitude / an internal comparison, respectively.

findings.quote: NVIDIA is led by co-founder Jensen Huang (Jen-Hsun Huang), its President and CEO
findings.issue: The grounding surface does not establish that Huang co-founded NVIDIA. The proxy lists him as "Jen-Hsun Huang, President and CEO"; the company description says only "Founded in 1993." "Co-founder" is a biographical claim absent from the pack.
findings.fix: Drop "co-founder" and use "President and CEO," as the proxy states, unless the descriptor can be grounded in a captured source.
findings.note: Addressed. "co-founder" is removed; leadership reads "NVIDIA is led by Jensen Huang (Jen-Hsun Huang), its President and CEO."

findings.quote: the segment grew as the latest generation shipped
findings.issue: No Gaming-specific growth figure is on the surface: the segment block gives only FY26 Gaming revenue $16B (7.4% of revenue), with no prior-year or quarterly Gaming growth, and the transcript does not break out Gaming. The claim that Gaming "grew" is unsupported.
findings.fix: Remove "grew as the latest generation shipped," or state only what the pack carries (FY26 Gaming $16B, 7.4% of revenue) without asserting growth.
findings.note: Addressed. The "grew as the latest generation shipped" clause is gone; the Gaming body no longer asserts a specific segment growth figure (the qualitative "grows far more slowly than the AI business" is a defensible counter given the 7.4% vs 89.7% mix).

findings.quote: The July 2026 selloff, which erased hundreds of billions of NVIDIA's value in a day, showed how quickly sentiment can turn.
findings.issue: The only surface support for the selloff is the Headlines block (2026-07-27/28): "NVDA Down 6% in Two Days," a broad Asia/SK Hynix chip sell-off, and "Apple Overtakes Nvidia as World's Most Valuable Company." The drop was about 6% over TWO days, not "in a day." "Hundreds of billions ... erased" is a computed magnitude (roughly 6% of the $5.14T market cap) the surface never states, and the authoring contract bars computing new figures. The claim is load-bearing: the same selloff is cited to justify the 25% bear weight and the "reverse hard"/"violent" language in thesis, scenarioCommentary and the bear driver.
findings.fix: Recast to what the headlines carry: a sharp roughly 6% two-day slide in late July 2026 amid a broad chip sell-off, after which Apple overtook NVIDIA as the most valuable company. Drop "in a day" (the source says two days) and the "hundreds of billions" figure, or state the move only as the headlines report it.
findings.note: Addressed. risks.idiosyncratic[0] reads "The July 2026 chip selloff, in which NVIDIA and its peers fell sharply, showed how quickly sentiment can turn." The "hundreds of billions ... in a day" magnitude and single-day framing are gone; "fell sharply" matches the headlines (NVDA -6% over two days, SK Hynix -15%).

findings.quote: committing capital to the AI build-out itself, taking stakes in customers and partners and backing financing platforms and data-center leases that support demand for its chips
findings.issue: This sentence is duplicated near-verbatim in cashflowCommentary ("committing capital to the AI build-out itself, investing in customers and partners and backing financing platforms and data-center leases that support demand for its chips"), and the same strategic-capital narrative is stated a third time in management.capitalAllocation ("deploying capital into the AI ecosystem itself, taking stakes in AI labs, backing financing platforms and signing long data-center leases to secure capacity for its customers"). Rubric 7: introduce a claim once and refer back in words; near-identical sentences should not appear across three sections (the token lint missed it because "taking"/"investing" differ). balanceCommentary even appends "as the cash-flow section describes" yet still restates the whole list.
findings.fix: Keep the substantive statement once, in cashflowCommentary where the circular-financing crux is argued. In balanceCommentary and capitalAllocation refer back in words (e.g., "the strategic commitments the cash-flow section details") instead of re-listing stakes in customers, financing platforms and data-center leases.
findings.note: Now addressed. management.capitalAllocation no longer re-lists the commitments; it refers back in words ("as the cash-flow section describes, NVIDIA is now deploying significant capital into the AI ecosystem itself to secure capacity and demand for its chips"). The stakes / financing-platforms / data-center-leases list appears once, in cashflowCommentary; balanceCommentary points in words.

findings.quote: it more than doubled year-over-year in the second quarter
findings.issue: The surface gives no Data Center year-over-year growth figure for Q2. The transcript carries Data Center Q2 revenue of $89B up 18% quarter-over-quarter, ACIE $40B up 138% YoY, and hyperscale $49B up 13% sequentially; the only "more than doubled"/+106% YoY figure is TOTAL company Q2 revenue ($96,221M vs $46,743M). Attaching "more than doubled year-over-year" to the Data Center segment attributes a total-company growth rate to one segment - an inference the pack invites but does not make, since the segment's own YoY (which depends on last year's Data Center mix) is not disclosed and is not certainly above 100%.
findings.fix: State what the surface carries for the segment - Data Center Q2 revenue of $89B, up 18% sequentially - or attribute the "more than doubled" (+106% YoY) to total company revenue rather than to Data Center. Do not assert a segment YoY the pack does not give.
findings.note: Now addressed. The Data Center body drops "more than doubled year-over-year in the second quarter" and reads "it grew again in the second quarter, as the growth section details." Growth point 1 grounds this to the transcript (Data Center revenue $89B in Q2, +18% sequentially); the +138% YoY is correctly attributed to ACIE, not the segment.

findings.issue: The identical clause "financial risk is essentially nil" appears twice in balanceCommentary - first paragraph ("interest coverage over 400 times, so financial risk is essentially nil") and second paragraph ("On the balance sheet alone, financial risk is essentially nil, which gives management the freedom to invest through a cycle"). Rubric 9 bars a tic repeated past the point of notice; the same conclusion in the same short field, verbatim, reads as a repeated tic.
findings.fix: State the conclusion once (first paragraph) and, in the second, refer to it in words - e.g., "with the balance sheet no constraint, management has the freedom to invest through a cycle" - rather than repeating "financial risk is essentially nil."
findings.note: Now addressed. "financial risk is essentially nil" appears once (para 1); para 2 now reads "On the balance sheet alone, there is little to worry about, which gives management the freedom to invest through a cycle."

findings.issue: Nothing in the Facts or Context blocks addresses autonomous-driving deployment timelines. The pack carries Automotive only as FY26 revenue $2.3B (1.1% of revenue) and the company description's in-vehicle-computing and autonomous-driving product lines; neither the MD&A, the transcript nor the headlines say the autonomy timeline is delayed. "the autonomy timeline keeps slipping" is a statement of fact the grounding surface does not support (Rubric 2), offered as a reason the segment is a modest contributor. It is non-load-bearing color in the smallest segment, so Minor rather than Critical, but the claim rests on neither a figure nor a quoted fact.
findings.fix: Drop "the autonomy timeline keeps slipping," or replace it with a grounded counter - the segment's small scale (1.1% of revenue, $2.3B) and its reliance on a multi-year design-win pipeline - rather than asserting an industry timeline the pack does not carry.
